notes: The RunPod management calls work from the web version now, the Android app delivers multi-select pictures to the Pose library, the install script refuses to fill a pod's own disk, and Settings has been tidied. RunPod's management API never answers the CORS preflight a browser sends before a request carrying an API key, so from the website every pod rental and volume listing died as "Failed to fetch" with nothing to diagnose. The site now hosts a small relay at /api/runpod that forwards each call, with your own key riding it and never stored, and hands back RunPod's answer word for word, so a failure now says which status and message came back. The Android app loads from its bundled file and can call RunPod directly, as it always has, with the relay as its fallback. The Pose library's Add button on Android chose pictures that never arrived: the framework's helper reads only the single picked file, and a multi-select picker returns its choices elsewhere, so the page got nothing. The wrapper now collects all of them, and answers the page on cancel too. The copy-and-paste install script checks that /workspace is a mounted network volume before downloading anything, since a pod deployed without the volume still has a /workspace of its own that fills in minutes and vanishes with the pod, and a leftover half-download is removed rather than resumed into, which means a download killed at the deadline starts over. Settings: the version in the header comes from one constant and is right; stale mentions of a "Change model" row are gone and the footer names all three photo engines; the Your own GPU intro describes what it does today; the Pose library has one entry point under Features; the five checks share a Diagnostics section with one answer box, and purging stuck vision jobs lives under Troubleshooting logs; Kontext and the vision model name sit behind a collapsed Advanced disclosure, as does the Photo Lab's picture-reference row; the Lab's face-pass box starts from the Settings toggle; LoRA help text stopped talking about pose LoRAs; Civitai favourites has one button, on the character card. The face pass, still unverified live, now logs the picture size and the face box in both the model's coordinates and the picture's, so the next run settles it from the logs alone.
